assumptions_made: This experiment uses synthetic data generated with a fixed seed to ensure reproducibility and consistency across runs
The synthetic dataset contains both informative features (linear combinations of others) and noise features to simulate realistic tabular data scenarios
Five seeds per ensemble size provide sufficient variance estimation for the analysis
The ensemble size sweep covers a reasonable range to detect diminishing returns
Computational resources allow full parameter sweep within the time limit

results.hypothesis: Test whether ensemble size has diminishing returns for tabular classification accuracy.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: A single decision stump on the same split.
results.success_criteria: Accuracy gains fall below 0.005 per doubling beyond some ensemble size, and that size is identified.
results.notes: Diminishing returns detected at 4 estimators. Accuracy gain per doubling fell below 0.005.
results.methodological_validity: synthetic surrogate data — the pipeline is exercised but the findings are NOT interpretable as evidence for or against the hypothesis
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
